\begin{center}{\Large\bf 12429 -- Finding Magic Triplets}\end{center}

Given a positive integer $n$ and a modulus $k$, count the number of triplets $(a, b, c)$ such that
$1 \le a \le b \le c \le n$ and $a + b^2 \equiv c^3 \pmod{k}$. This is a fairly long paragraph so that the
text wraps over several lines and we can check that lines are joined back into a single paragraph,
including hyphen-
ated words.

A second paragraph starts here. The string $s$ consists of lowercase letters only.

\section*{Input}
The first line contains an integer $T$ ($1 \le T \le 50$), the number of test cases. Each test case consists of two integers $n$ and $k$ where $1 \le n, k \le 10^5$.

\section*{Output}
For each test case, print ``Case $x$: $y$'' where $x$ is the case number and $y$ is the answer.

\section*{Sample Input}
\begin{verbatim}
2
10 7
1 1
\end{verbatim}

\section*{Sample Output}
\begin{verbatim}
Case 1: 27
Case 2: 1
\end{verbatim}
